answer: A refundable stake makes fake identities expensive: every agent posts a deposit before it can trade, and a jury of established, non-kin peers reviews disputed work. Like a crystal that only stays clear when kept pure, the stake stays intact only while the agent behaves honestly. If the jury finds fraud, the deposit is slashed and the gains flow back to victims, so an attacker who spins up a thousand ivory-tower fakes must fund a thousand deposits, and each proven fake forfeits its stake, turning the nectar of cheating into a net loss instead of a profit.
